messages.author: e17dc21aa6c006ab
messages.subject: Empatica CSV File Error
parts:
Dear All, 

I am trying to process the empatica CSV file, which is basically three days of recording for sleep analysis. i am using the readmyacccsv function to process the file but have this error and trying to figure out where the problem ?


I am wondering if it's a problem with Sampling frequency, since empoatics have 64 sampling frequency, whereas other accelerometers work with 1Hz, i am wondering if this is a problem related to sampling frequency or something else.?

looking forward to hearing from you. 

Kind regards,

Abdul Haleem

here is my script

library(GGIR)

             mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),
             datadir="empatica_data.csv",

             studyname = "Empatica",

             rmc.dec = ".",

             rmc.col.acc = 2:4,
             #rmc.col.temp = 5,
             rmc.col.time=1,
             rmc.unit.acc = "g",
            # rmc.unit.temp = "C",
             rmc.unit.time = "POSIXct",
             rmc.format.time = "%d/%m/%Y %H:%M:%OS",
             rmc.desiredtz = "Europe/Brussels",
             rmc.configtz = NULL,
             rmc.sf = 64,
             rmc.noise = 0.013
             )
and csv file as well.

Regards,

Abdul Haleem

messages.author: 05de4f382b390d3d
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Empatica CSV File Error
parts:
Hi,

Thanks! I found a minor bug in GGIR that triggered the error that you were experiencing. You can try to install the branch issue1032_bugDuplicatesCalibration in which I tried to give a solution to your issue:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("wadpac/GGIR", ref = "issue1032_bugDuplicatesCalibration")

However, this might not be enough, note that the accelerations in your csv file do not seem to be in g units, but you are specifying that rmc.acc.unit = "g". The values in your csv seem very high to be g units, make sure what unit of measurement the empatica has, I am not sure of that.

Best,
Jairo
